---
title: "Sparse support, indexing, and gating"
---

This facility separates logical support, candidate retrieval, conditional
activation, latent-state computation, and physical execution. Its first
consumers are controlled event-stream and ranked-gene embedding examples.
They are engineering fixtures and do not establish biological validity.

## Native responsibilities

`Cellerator::sparse_support` is a Torch-free host library. Public contracts live
under `Cellerator/compute/support`, `indexing`, and `gating`.

- Logical support retains stable relation and edge identities, ordered
  participant roles and multiplicity, and immutable structure epochs.
- Reverse postings implement exact any/all retrieval and sorted set
  intersections. Temporal indexes preserve repeated occurrences and filter
  ordinal or timestamp windows before returning candidates.
- Condition programs share predicates across logical edges. Sparse dirty
  updates and cross-cell bitmaps produce distinct primal and derivative work
  sets. Capacity failures are explicit; query output is not silently truncated.
- Bounded proposals use existing neighborhoods and seeded exploration. The
  proposal budget bounds search effort, rather than fixing eligible degree.
  A proposal is not evidence of a biological or causal relationship.

The CUDA component supplies device posting retrieval, condition bitmaps, and
work-set construction. Its initial sparse merge/compaction schedules are exact
baselines; algorithm choice requires complete-cost evidence.

## Latent state and learned gates

The numerical operation layer provides indexed latent transitions
`z_next = tanh(A z + B u + b)` and explicit VJPs. Cells have independent state
over overlapping mechanisms, with model parameters shared across cells.
There is no required chromatin annotation or predefined biological mechanism
ontology. Event order, gene identity, rank, and event occurrence identity remain
distinct.

The initial gate uses `p = sigmoid(score / temperature)` and pruned forward
`q = p * (p >= threshold)`. Soft training can precede fine-tuning with the
declared estimator `q_train = p + stop_gradient(q - p)`. This estimator keeps
sigmoid gradients for selected derivative candidates, including candidates
omitted from the primal. It is a biased gradient estimator. Finite differences
of the discontinuous pruned computation do not validate that estimator.

The derivative candidate policy is part of the model contract and checkpoint.
Scoring and derivative-only work must be included in training costs. Structural
pruning, numerical gating, and physical packing are separate operations.
The native cyclic sampler retains all admitted interactions and bounds only
the additional dormant sample. Its seed, rotation counter, coverage counts,
and biased estimator policy are explicit; unvisited candidates have no exact
gradient claim.

FP16 storage/multiplication and FP32 accumulation, gradients, and master
parameters are the initial mixed-precision route. An explicit FP32 reference
remains available. No BF16 or TF32 hardware support is assumed.

## Geometry and the Torch boundary

The initial packed numerical backend uses the existing CE-GEO physical cover,
logical value maps, and width-64 consumer. A prepared projection binds logical
IDs to physical slots; per-cell activity determines which tiles execute.
Irregular support retains a sparse SIMT route. Physical packing is replaceable
and does not redefine logical support or learned parameter identity.

Compiled native operations participate in Torch training through explicit
custom backward operations. One canonical native parameter owner exposes a
stable Torch leaf and uses guarded Adam publication. Shared scorer parameters
allow new support records without adding per-edge optimizer tensors.

Support/projection epochs stay fixed while forward tapes are live. The
adaptive support manager stages additions, revocations, and delta-to-base
promotions, then publishes between training windows. A stable compiled base
and adaptation delta have disjoint logical ownership. The adaptation delta is
different from the CE-GEO physical MMA residual region.

High-confidence compilation fixes routing and storage; state-dependent gates
remain evaluable. Checkpoints retain logical support, owner and optimizer
state, application/window state, proposal RNG, gate policy, and physical
preparation metadata. Restore logical state before rebuilding physical views.

## Applications and evidence

The event consumer uses occurrence and window indexes before scoring and
updates affected latent mechanisms in caller-defined order. Expiration changes
temporal eligibility without reversing earlier recurrent updates. Timestamp
windows do not impose a continuous-time transition law.

The ranked consumer intersects selected gene identities with support and keeps
rank as a separate feature. A masked token contributes neither an entity nor a
rank embedding. Ranked position does not imply temporal order.

Native pointer-based CUDA APIs use caller-owned reserved storage and streams.
The synthetic Torch consumers currently build some worksets on the CPU and
explicitly transfer gate decisions for host sampling. Their mechanism postings
are refreshed after parameter publication. Those costs are separate from the
allocation-free numerical launch contract; these examples do not establish a
fully device-resident training pipeline.

See the [benchmark protocol](../bench/sparse_support/README.md) and
[implementation contract](sparse_support_foundation/draft.md). Retained
qualification distinguishes host tests, admitted GPU correctness, numerical
and surrogate-gradient comparisons, learning behavior, sanitizers, profiling,
and unprofiled timings. Preparation, discovery, gating, packing, backward,
publication, and memory remain visible in complete-cost comparisons. No single
layout or algorithm is the default winner for every workload.

The source-bound [native qualification](../bench/sparse_support/evidence/qualification/native/README.md),
[corrected gradient/lifecycle run](../bench/sparse_support/evidence/qualification/lifecycle/v9-gradient-scatter/REPORT.md),
and [learning fixture report](../bench/sparse_support/evidence/qualification/learning/v9_corrected/REPORT.md)
retain the exact tested snapshots. The corrected 50-epoch fixture reached
56.25% ranked-gene accuracy with pruned execution versus 34.38% for shuffled
support. Event accuracy was 28.12% on 64 held-out cells, close to the four-class
chance rate of 25%; this is a weak result and does not establish recovery of the
hidden mechanisms. The earlier run with incorrectly scattered sampled gate
gradients remains diagnostic evidence and is excluded from those results.
The [final snapshot-restoration suite](../bench/sparse_support/evidence/qualification/lifecycle/v11-snapshot-restore/REPORT.md)
passes 28 tests, including loading into a fresh model after a novel edge was
promoted and later revoked. Saved base/delta ownership, epochs, tombstones, and
promotion evidence are restored directly while retaining the parameter leaf.

The [balanced V100 comparison](../bench/sparse_support/evidence/experiments/packed_training_v9_confirmation/run_001/REPORT.md)
found no reliable complete-cost advantage for packed execution on its two
small relation fixtures. Same-process paired training favored SIMT by about
2.5%; the separate-request KDA comparison disagreed and its aggregate interval
crossed parity. SIMT remains the measured fallback. Packed execution is a
qualified trainable capability, without a promoted performance regime here.
